title: Fundraising Ideas for Sports Teams (2026)
verdict: The best fundraising ideas for sports teams have one thing in common: people get something they want. Team gear, a sponsor's name on a jersey and a well-run event will out-raise a bake sale for the same effort.
Here are twelve ideas that work, grouped by how much work they take, with notes on what to watch for.

cta.text: See how a Fan Shop works

list: Online team store. Supporters buy hoodies, shirts and hats. The team earns a share of each sale, and nobody handles cash or boxes.
Jersey sponsor. A local business pays to have its logo on the jersey or warmup. One good sponsor can cover the uniforms.
Restaurant night. A local restaurant gives a percentage of one evening's sales to the team.
Crowdfunding page. Good for a specific goal such as a tournament trip. Share it with a deadline.
Banner sponsors. Sell banner space at your field or gym for the season.
Skills clinic. Older players run a morning camp for younger kids.
Shoot-a-thon or hit-a-thon. Players collect pledges per basket or hit.
Car wash. Still works, especially with a sponsor matching the take.
Host a tournament. Entry fees and concessions add up. It needs fields, referees and volunteers.
Golf outing. Popular with parents and sponsors. Plan months ahead.
Raffle or auction. Collect donated prizes. Check your state's rules on raffles first.
Discount cards. Local businesses offer deals on a card the team sells.

Best for
rows: Clubs with field or gym access

list: Name the goal and the number. People give to a new set of uniforms, not to a general fund.
Set a deadline of two weeks or less.
Make it easy to pay online.
Keep one person in charge of the money, and report the total.

why: Two of these ideas run through Wooter. A Fan Shop is a free online team store where families and supporters buy team gear and the team earns a commission, which Wooter says is often 10 to 50 percent. Wooter handles the orders, production and shipping.
The other is the sponsor jersey. A sponsor's logo can be added to the jersey design, and the design work is free.

faq.q: What is the easiest fundraiser for a sports team?
faq.a: An online team store or a jersey sponsor. Neither needs volunteers on a Saturday.
A business pays the team, and its logo goes on the jersey, warmup or banner. Check your league's rules on sponsor logos first.

faq.q: How much can a team store raise?
faq.a: It depends on how many people buy. Wooter says Fan Shop commissions are often 10 to 50 percent of sales.

faq.q: Do we need permission to run a raffle?
faq.a: Often yes. Raffle rules vary by state, so check before selling tickets.

faq.q: How do we ask a business to sponsor us?
faq.a: Ask in person, name a specific amount and say exactly what they get: logo placement, a banner, a thank-you post.
